APPLICATION 06 / TRACE

Penstock Inspection Robots & ROVs

Long, steep and enclosed. Plan the whole route.

Penstocks and pressure conduits combine steep gradients, long enclosed routes and limited access. Robotic inspection needs a route-specific assessment of vehicle, tether and recovery.

Home / Applications / Penstock & pressure conduit inspection

Who this is for

Hydropower owners, penstock maintenance teams and specialist inspection contractors.

Project inputs

  • Conduit length, diameter and longitudinal profile
  • Flooded or dewatered condition and flow during inspection
  • Access points and launch arrangements
  • Features to inspect and the position reference required
Build a project brief

The short answer

Penstock inspection robots must handle steep gradients, bends and long enclosed routes. For long flooded conduits, a long-distance tunnel ROV such as the AD-400 is the starting point; shorter accessible sections may suit an inspection ROV like the R-45. Plan the tether, position reference and recovery for the actual profile.

01

Establish whether the conduit stays flooded

A flooded penstock can be inspected by an ROV; a dewatered one may suit a crawler or a person with rope access instead. Clarify the condition, the access points and the inspection window before choosing equipment.

02

Map gradient, bends and diameter

Steep inclines, bends, bifurcations and diameter changes affect tether drag, vehicle control and recovery. Provide the longitudinal profile and the location of every transition.

03

Match the platform to the route length

For long flooded conduits, the AD-400 is designed for distances measured in kilometres. Shorter or more accessible sections may suit an inspection ROV such as the R-45 with the right tether package.

04

Decide what the inspection must measure

Lining condition, corrosion, coating damage, joints and deposits call for different lighting, camera and sonar setups. Agree the required features and how their position along the conduit will be referenced.

05

Engineer the recovery plan

Agree what happens if the tether snags, communication is lost or flow changes. Recovery equipment, access and responsibilities must be defined before launch.

BEFORE YOU SPECIFY

Frequently asked questions.

Is the AD-400 suitable for every penstock?

No. Penstocks vary widely in gradient, diameter and flow. Treat each conduit as a separate engineering review and confirm the proposed configuration against its profile.

Can a penstock be inspected without dewatering?

An ROV inspects in water, so a flooded penstock can be inspected without dewatering if flow and isolation arrangements allow safe operation.
